narrative.overview: Locust Studio is a desktop workbench for engineers who read numbers. Scenario on the left, the work in the middle, the console on the right. It is dense but calm: panels separate by tone, not by lines, and the only loud things on screen are the Run button, the live status and a failure count above zero. Two themes share one structure: Graphite (dark, default) and Paper (light, warm off-white for bright rooms and report screenshots).
keyCharacteristics: Two themes, one structure: Graphite dark (default) and Paper light
Inter for the chrome, JetBrains Mono with tabular figures for every measured number
One accent per theme, used on the primary action, the selected state and focus
Flat, tonal layering; no shadows at rest
Numbers right-aligned; red appears only when a failure count is above zero

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each theme has one accent. It goes on the primary action, the active tab, focus and nothing decorative.

rules.name: The Earned Red Rule
rules.body: A zero is plain ink. Red appears only on a failure count above zero or a failure share, so red on screen always means something failed.

rules.name: The Measured-Number Rule
rules.body: Every value that came from a run or a count uses the mono face with tabular figures and is right-aligned. Names and labels never use the mono face.

rules.name: The Tone-Not-Line Rule
rules.body: Separate areas with a tonal step first. A border appears only between the three panes, under table rows and around inputs.

dos: Do right-align every number in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do keep one accent per theme: Signal Indigo in Graphite, Ledger Teal in Paper.
Do separate areas with tone (window, panel, raised) before reaching for a border.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 or better: muted text uses the muted token, never a lighter grey.
donts: Don't colour a zero failure count red.
Don't use decorative gradients, glassmorphism or glow.
Don't put a 1px border around every panel; the old look did this.
Don't add icons where a text label suffices.
Don't animate metric values beyond a plain update each second.
